subject: Post-call recap: input/output window impact on latency & scaling
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Romero <alex@finndo.com>, Priya Shah <priya@finndo.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-21T15:12:00Z
Subject: Post-call recap: input/output window impact on latency & scaling

Alex / Priya — thanks again for the conversation earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared picture of latency and token-window constraints that came up on the call:

- Goals you called out:
  - P95 generation latency target: ~200ms for short responses (<=128 output tokens) under normal load.
  - Sustained throughput target: 400–600 qps with occasional spikes to 1k qps for short bursts.
  - Streaming required for progressive response UI; network-level chunking acceptable but want per-chunk latency <120ms.

- Context window constraints we discussed:
  - Typical input size: 3–6k tokens (user history + product state).
  - Max output expectations: up to 1.5k tokens in long-form summarization jobs (not the interactive path).
  - Primary concern: long input + long output pushes model into non-streamable paths and increases per-token latency due to KV cache growth and attention compute.

Immediate next steps I propose: 
1) You share the brief latency/throughput doc you mentioned (attachments below) — we can map that to model families and quantization profiles.
2) Redwood to run a focused perf matrix: assess P95 vs input-window buckets (<=1k / 1k-3k / >3k tokens) for the interactive model variant + streaming enabled. Aim to deliver preliminary numbers in 3 business days.
3) Align on a demo that shows streaming with incremental output slices for a 3k input / 512 output case. Redwood to provide a lightweight harness and suggested test vectors.

I'll loop Sean and Laura here to own the perf run and the demo setup. If that plan looks good, I'll schedule a 45-minute technical sync for Wed morning.

Thanks —
Grace O'Connor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0187

             redwood_demo_agenda_v2.pdf (proposed agenda),
             perf_test_harness_spec.csv (test vectors stub)

From: Alex Romero <alex@finndo.com>

Cc: Priya Shah <priya@finndo.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-21T17:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: input/output window impact on latency & scaling

Thanks Grace — this is exactly the right framing. A few clarifications from our side:

- The 200ms P95 target is for the interactive UI flows (<=128 token outputs). For the long-form batch summarization (1k–1.5k outputs) we expect latency in the 1–3s range but throughput matters more there.
- Bursts to 1k qps are typically bursts across many short requests (many users), not single very large requests. That makes batching behavior and concurrency very important.
- Streaming expectations: we want partial tokens to arrive ASAP; if the platform can surface incremental tokens at ~50–100ms intervals that'd be ideal for UX.

Attaching the doc I referenced (finndo_latency_requirements.pdf) — it includes sample traces and our synthetic load profile.

Also: are there recommended model families on Redwood that support 4k+ context comfortably while still allowing streaming? If streaming is incompatible with large KV growth, we need to know whether to accept a smaller working context for interactive flows and route long-form jobs to a different service/model.

—Alex
Alex Romero
Head of Platform Engineering, Finndo Systems
alex@finndo.com

Date: 2026-08-21T20:26:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: input/output window impact on latency & scaling

Alex — thanks for the doc, received and skimmed. Quick answers inline and a proposal for the perf matrix: 

- Recommended model families: we have two sensible paths.
  1) Interactive path (low-latency streaming): 1k context-capable variants with aggressive KV-cache optimizations and streaming-friendly kernels. These hit the 150–250ms P95 for <=128-token outputs at ~500 qps in our baseline runs.
  2) Long-window path (4k+ contexts): variants optimized for accuracy and larger KV footprint; these typically increase per-token latency by ~25–45% depending on sequence length and are often non-trivial to stream for very long outputs.

- Proposal for perf matrix (deliverable in 3 business days):
  - Test axes: model variant x input-window bucket x output-size bucket x concurrency level (1 / 50 / 200 / 500 concurrent requests)
  - Metrics: P50/P95/P99 generation latency, tokens/sec/core, memory footprint, streaming chunk turnaround time, and tail stalls when KV cache grows.
  - Deliverable: CSV of aggregated metrics + a small writeup with recommended routing (interactive vs batch) and fallback hedges.

If that sounds good I'll kick off the runs tomorrow. Also propose a demo slot Thu 9am PT — Laura, Sean, does that work for you for the joint call?

Best,
Grace

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: input/output window impact on latency & scaling

I'll run the perf matrix and prototype harness today. Notes for the team and deliverables: 

- Run plan: start with the interactive model variant at 1k-context profile. Buckets: <=1k, 1k–3k, >3k input; outputs: 64, 256, 1024 tokens. Concurrency sweep at 1/50/200/500.
- Environment: dedicated instance group (NVIDIA A10x2) to reduce noisy neighbor variance; we'll also run smaller mixed tests on shared infra to emulate your production burst behavior.
- Streaming check: instrument chunk emit times and measure first-byte and subsequent chunk intervals; include a trace for a sample 3k in / 512 out job.
- I'll attach the initial harness and a short run script after the first pass: perf_test_harness_spec.csv and redwood_demo_agenda_v2.pdf will be updated with concrete times.

I'll post results to the linked Drive folder and ping the HubSpot deal. If all looks good we can demo Thu 9am PT.

—Sean
